Post Date: 2017-03-31T00:02:57Z

Title: Problems building library with Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard for Core 1.1
Description: I have a library I am building for Core 1.0, and it builds fine:
```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0-*",

  "dependencies": {
    "Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client": "5.2.3",
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures": "1.0.0",
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Runtime": "1.0.0",
    "NETStandard.Library": "1.6.0",
    "Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard":  "2.3.6" 
  },

  "frameworks": {
    "netstandard1.6": {
      "imports": [ "dnxcore50", "portable-net451+win8" ]
    }
  }
}
```

To update to Core 1.1, the project.json is updated:
```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0-*",

  "dependencies": {
    "Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client": "5.2.3",
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures": "1.1.1",
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Runtime": "1.1.0",
    "NETStandard.Library": "1.6.1",
    "Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard": "2.3.6"
  },

  "frameworks": {
    "netstandard1.6": {
      "imports": [ "portable-net462+win8" ]
    }
  }
}
```

I'll analyze this GitHub issue to determine if a build environment is needed to verify the solution.

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about package compatibility problems when upgrading from .NET Core 1.0 to 1.1. The problem is clearly described in the error logs: certain dependencies (System.Net.WebSockets 4.3.0 and System.Collections.Specialized 4.3.0) only support .NETStandard 1.3, not 1.6. 

The solution to this issue would involve modifying the project.json file to either:
1. Target netstandard1.3 instead of netstandard1.6
2. Use a different version of the Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard package that's compatible with netstandard1.6
3. Add appropriate package version constraints

This is a package dependency/compatibility issue that can be verified through analysis of the NuGet package metadata and project configuration. An expert can determine the correct solution by examining the package dependencies and compatibility information without needing to build the project. The error messages already provide the necessary information about which packages are incompatible and why.
